{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BfDmud6WSdQiaoK9e2QyQR","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tFROM python:3.11-bookworm\n2\t\n3\tRUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git curl build-essential libffi-dev libssl-dev \\\n4\t && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*\n5\t\n6\tWORKDIR /app\n7\t\n8\t# Clone, pin to base commit, strip .git (anti-cheat: agent cannot inspect fix PR/future history).\n9\t# Re-init a single base commit + immutable tag so the verifier can reset test files;\n10\t# git apply still works without upstream history.\n11\t# Bug patches live OUTSIDE assets/ — assets/ is copied wholesale to an agent-readable\n12\t# path below, so anything parked in it is shipped to the model. They land in /tmp only\n13\t# long enough to be applied to the base snapshot, and the same RUN deletes them: the\n14\t# reverse of a bug patch is the fix, and /tmp is as agent-visible as /app.\n15\tCOPY bugs/ /tmp/bugs/\n16\tRUN git clone https://github.com/Textualize/textual /app \\\n17\t && git -C /app checkout 5cb6cd03746afce553c88ab07362130a8880369a \\\n18\t && rm -rf /app/.git \\\n19\t && for p in /tmp/bugs/*.patch; {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_013hq3ucENGBd3dRJnw6oroV","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t#!/usr/bin/env python3\n2\t\"\"\"Reward computation for Textualize__textual-5386-mm.\n3\t\n4\tParses the JUnit XML report emitted by test.sh and computes the reward from\n5\tconfig.json's f2p/p2p lists. NEVER inspects candidate source — only the test report.\n6\t\n7\tReward policy — BINARY, no partial credit:\n8\t  1.0  -- every f2p test passes AND every p2p test still passes.\n9\t  0.0  -- anything else: a strict subset of f2p passing, a p2p regression, or\n10\t          no report at all. A half-fix is unsolved, and the f2p/p2p count keys\n11\t          in reward.json carry how close it got.\n12\t\"\"\"\n13\timport json\n14\timport os\n15\timport re\n16\timport sys\n17\timport xml.etree.ElementTree as ET\n18\t\n19\tCONF = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))\n20\tF2P, P2P = CONF['f2p'], CONF['p2p']\n21\tREPORT = '/logs/verifier/report.xml'\n22\t\n23\t# --- canonical reward writer + --rubric gate ------------------------------------\n24\t# Copied from template/tests/verifier_reward_block.py. reward.json MUST be a FLAT map\n25\t# of numbers with exactly these seven keys — harbor parses it as\n26\t# VerifierResult.rewards: dict[str, float | int] and takes it in PREFERENCE to\n27\t# reward.txt. A nested dict, list, string or None raises a pydantic ValidationError\n28\t# that aborts the trial BEFORE any reward is recorded, while reward.txt still gets\n29\t# written inside the container — so the run looks scored when harbor stored nothing.\n30\t#   rubric_passed: 1 pass / 0 fail / -1 not graded.\n31\t# Registered with atexit so it writes LAST.\n32\t\n33\timport atexit, json as _cj, os as _co, sys as _cs\n34\t\n35\t_CANON_JSON = \"/logs/verifier/reward.json\"\n36\t_CANON_TXT = \"/logs/verifier/reward.txt\"\n37\t_canon = {}\n38\t\n39\t\n40\tdef canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):\n41\t    \"\"\"THE reward policy for the whole corpus. BINARY -- there is no partial credit.\n42\t\n43\t    tests_passed is 1.0 only when every f2p test passes AND every p2p test still passes. identifiers in config.json are\n        # \"path/to/file.py::test_name\" -- match tolerantly against both forms below.\n        full = f\"{classname}::{name}\".strip(':')\n        failed = any(c.tag in ('failure', 'error') for c in tc)\n        skipped = any(c.tag == 'skipped' for c in tc)\n        results[full] = 'skip' if skipped else ('fail' if failed else 'pass')\n    return results\n\n\ndef matched(idents, results):\n    \"\"\"Match each configured identifier against reported test names (substring tolerant,\n    since junitxml classnames use dotted module paths, e.g. tests.snapshot_tests.test_snapshots).\"\"\"\n    out = {}\n    for ident in idents:\n        test_name = ident.split('::')[-1]\n        hit = None\n        for k, v in results.items():\n            if ident in k or k.endswith(f\"::{test_name}\") or re.search(re.escape(test_name), k):\n                hit = v\n                break\n        out[ident] = hit or 'missing'\n    return out\n\n\ndef main():\n    results = load_results()\n    f2p = matched(F2P, results)\n    p2p = matched(P2P, results)\n    f2p_pass = [k for k, v in f2p.items() if v == 'pass']\n    p2p_pass = [k for k, v in p2p.items() if v == 'pass']\n\n    reward = canon_reward(len(f2p_pass), len(F2P),\n                          len(p2p_pass), len(P2P),\n                          rubric_verdict(sys.argv[1:]))\n\n    # Per-test detail rides along as extra SCALAR keys on the same flat dict (never a nested\n    # map, which harbor's pydantic parse would reject). Nothing here asserts a\n+behaviour that the captures do not show, uses a trigger they do not name, or inspects a\n+property that is not visible in them.\n+\n+Capture 1 shows six strips of blocks: the first strip has its end block filled red, the\n+second has its start block filled teal, the third has its \"off\" block filled grey, the\n+fourth has its \"pinned\" block filled blue, the fifth is filled purple end to end, and the\n+sixth has its \"flagged\" block filled amber. Capture 2 is the same screen after the window\n+went behind another window and came back: the red, teal, grey, blue and purple fills are\n+gone and those blocks are drawn like their neighbours, while the amber one is unchanged.\n+\n+Everything is asserted against *resolved* style values read back from `widget.styles`\n+while the app runs headlessly under `App.run_test()`. These are the fills visible in capture 1.\n+IDLE_CSS = \"#1b2b44\"\n+RED_CSS = \"#e5484d\"\n+TEAL_CSS = \"#12a594\"\n+GREY_CSS = \"#5b6270\"\n+BLUE_CSS = \"#3e63dd\"\n+PURPLE_CSS = \"#8e4ec6\"\n+AMBER_CSS = \"#ffb224\"\n+TEXT_CSS = \"#e6e9ef\"\n+\n+IDLE = Color.parse(IDLE_CSS)\n+RED = Color.parse(RED_CSS)\n+TEAL = Color.parse(TEAL_CSS)\n+GREY = Color.parse(GREY_CSS)\n+BLUE = Color.parse(BLUE_CSS)\n+PURPLE = Color.parse(PURPLE_CSS)\n+AMBER = Color.parse(AMBER_CSS)\n+\n+\n+class Strip(Horizontal):\n+    \"\"\"One horizontal strip of blocks, as seen in the captures.\"\"\"\n+\n+\n+class Board(Vertical):\n+    \"\"\"The column the strips are stacked in.\"\"\"\n+\n+\n+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n+# Helpers\n+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n+def assert_fills(expected: Mapping[Widget, Color], context: str) -> None:\n+    \"\"\"Every block in `expected` is filled with exactly the colour mapped to it.\n+\n+    Pinning every block to a named fill, rather than only checking that the special ones\n+    are special, matters: a block that ended up with no fill at all must not be able to\n+    slip through as \"not highlighted\".\n+    \"\"\"\n+    wrong = {\n+        block: (block.styles.background, colour)\n+        for block, colour in expected.items()\n+        if block.styles.background != colour\n+    }\n+    assert not wrong, }}\n+    \"\"\"\n+    )\n+\n+    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:\n+        with Board():\n+            with Strip(id=\"strip-a\"):\n+                for text in (\"one\", \"two\", \"three\", Anti-band-aid: dropping the affected fills altogether, so that\n+    the screen is merely consistent, is not a fix.\"\"\"\n+    app = BoardApp()\n+    async with app.run_test(size=(100, 34)):\n+        assert_fills(board_expectation(app), \"as first drawn\")\n+\n+\n+async def test_flagged_block_is_the_one_that_is_never_affected():\n+    \"\"\"The amber fill on the \"flagged\" block is the same in both captures; it must stay\n+    that way, before and after any change here.\"\"\"\n+    app = BoardApp()\n+    async with app.run_test(size=(100, 34)) as pilot:\n+        strip = app.query_one(\"#strip-f\", Strip)\n+\n+        def expectation() -> dict[Widget, Color]:\n+            return {\n+                block: (AMBER if block.has_class(\"flagged\") else IDLE)\n+                for block in strip.children\n+            }\n+\n+        assert_fills(expectation(), \"as first drawn\")\n+        await window_goes_behind_and_returns(app, pilot)\n+        assert_fills(expectation(), \"after the window came back\")\n+\n+\n+async def test_scenario_is_non_vacuous():\n+    \"\"\"Guards against the screen degenerating into something the assertions hold for\n+    trivially.\"\"\"\n+    app = BoardApp()\n+    async with app.run_test(size=(100, 34)) as pilot:\n+        expected = board_expectation(app)\n+\n+        # The screen really does show the six different fills of capture 1, so neither\n+        # \"everything is idle\" nor \"everything is highlighted\" can satisfy it.\n+        assert len(set(expected.values())) == 7, (\n+            f\"scenario is broken: the screen only uses {set(expected.values())}\"\n+        )\n+\n+        # The strips whose fill depends on a block's position really do hold blocks that\n+        # nothing else tells apart: same type, no id, no marker.\n+        for strip_id in (\"strip-a\", \"strip-b\"):\n+            blocks = list(app.query_one(f\"#{strip_id}\", Strip).children)\n+            assert len(blocks) == 4\n+            assert len({type(block) for block in blocks}) == 1\n+            assert all(block.id is None and not block.classes for block in blocks)\n+\n+        # Every block really is painted after the window comes back -- the assertions are\n+        # not passing over blocks that were left blank.\n+        await window_goes_behind_and_returns(app, pilot)\n+        assert all(\n+            block.styles.background is not None for block in app.query(Label)\n+        ), \"some block ended up with no fill at all\"\n+\n+        with pytest.raises(NoMatches):\n+            app.query_one(\"#no-such-block-exists\")\n","numLines":409,"startLine":1,"totalLines":409}}}
